subject: Privatenet token-sync failures during canary — bridge & remediation
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@healthsync.io>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: <no subject> — intermittent reconnects during canary

Hi Naomi,

We started the canary for the privatenet upgrade at ~07:45 this morning (US-EAST). Around 08:00 we saw a spike of agent reconnects across three nodes and a bunch of 502s in our app logs. Our side shows a token sync failure in the agent logs: "token validation timeout" repeatedly. We rolled the canary back but wanted to surface immediately since this impacted a small set of customers.

I attached a small bundle of agent logs and a short snippet from our app showing the 502s.

Can we get a bridge with your infra/engineering team? We need a quick triage and an ETA for a root cause and remediation. We are running in a VPC with privatenet and this prevented some writes to our audit store.

Thanks,
Alex

(Attachment: healthsync_agent_logs_20261215.tgz)

--
Alex Dunn
Sr. SRE, HealthSync, Inc.
alex.dunn@healthsync.io

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: intermittent reconnects during canary — scheduling bridge

Alex,

Thanks for flagging and for the logs — I see the attachment. We're sorry for the disruption.

I've looped in our infra oncall (Irene) and the platform lead (Ben). We're standing up a short bridge at 09:00 ET to triage. Preliminary ask for the bridge:
- Can you share the private agent config (agent version + token refresh interval)?
- Any NAT/FLB changes on your side in the 07:30–08:10 window?

We'll try to identify whether this is a tokensync race, a token TTL miscalculation in our control plane, or an edge proxy regression introduced in the canary.

Bridge details (zoom): https://redwood.zoom.us/j/974312598 (will post recording)

Regards,
Naomi

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@healthsync.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: intermittent reconnects during canary — initial findings

Alex / Naomi,

Thanks for joining the bridge. Short summary of what we saw during the session:
- The control plane telemetry shows a burst of token validation latency starting at 07:58 UTC-05:00 tied to the canary cohort's new auth refresh handler.
- Agent-side logs in your bundle show repeated "token validation timeout" errors and immediate reconnect attempts (we correlated client nonce IDs).
- We reproduced a similar condition in a local staging canary by flipping the auth handler; root cause points to a change in the canary that increased auth validation path latency by ~220ms under burst, pushing some clients over the agent-side timeout.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Rolled the canary back to previous auth handler (completed 08:18 ET) — this stopped new failures.
- Applied a short-term increase to agent token validation timeout and added a retry window in the client to avoid immediate disconnect on transient validation spikes.

Next steps (short list):
1) Postmortem doc (draft) capturing timeline + telemetry (working on this now).
2) Backport an auth handler fix and add a safety circuit in the validation path to bound latency under burst.
3) Formalize a canary gating rule to reject canaries that increase auth validation p95 by >50ms.

We've attached initial evidence and logs. We'll circulate a full postmortem and patch plan tomorrow.

Irene

(Attachment: privnet_tokensync_evidence_20261215.tgz)

--
Irene Choi
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 17:40:00 -05:00
Subject: Postmortem and next steps — tokensync latency regression during canary

Alex,

Following up with the promised postmortem and next steps. Thank you for the fast rollback and for the logs you provided — they were instrumental to repro and correlation.

Summary:
- Impact: brief service disruption to a subset of your nodes during canary (07:58–08:18 ET, Dec 15), causing reconnects and transient 502s affecting writes to an audit store.
- Root cause: an auth validation handler change in the canary increased p95 validation latency and when combined with existing agent-side timeout settings led to immediate reconnects.
- Remediation completed: canary rollback, short-term increase of agent token timeout, client retry window, and staging backport patch queued.

Deliverables and timelines:
- Postmortem doc (attached draft): privnet_tokensync_postmortem_draft.docx — final by 2026-12-18.
- Patch to auth handler: ETA 2026-12-19 (QA + canary gating).
- Canary gating policy update: ETA 2027-01-05 (to add automated p95 checks).
- Credits/compensation: Our CS team can discuss a goodwill credit for the window; Naomi will follow up after internal review.

Attachments:
- privnet_tokensync_postmortem_draft.docx
- healthsync_agent_logs_20261215.tgz
- bridge-recording-20261215.mp4

Please let me know if you'd like a walkthrough of the postmortem or to schedule a deeper technical session with our platform team.

Thanks again,
Naomi
